reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the figure. O is the center, AB is the diameter (horizontal line). From O, several rays extend into the upper half-plane.

Angles shown: 20° between OB and the first ray; 30° between the first ray and the second ray; 35° between the second ray and the third ray; 40° between... let me look carefully.

Labels: 20° is near the B side, between diameter OB and the first ray (about 20° above horizontal). 30° is between the first ray and the second ray. 35° is between the second ray and the third ray (the orange ray bounding the shaded sector). 40° is between the ray on the left side of the shaded sector and OA? Wait, the 40° label is on the left, between the ray going toward the upper-left (the left boundary of the shaded sector) and OA (the leftward horizontal direction).

Actual figure: the shaded sector is between the orange ray (slightly right of vertical, about 85° from positive x-axis?) and the ray going upper-left (about 140°?). Let me set up coordinates: measure angles from the positive x-axis (OB direction) counterclockwise.

Rays: OB is 0°. First ray is 20°. Second ray is 20+30=50°. Third ray is 50+35=85°. This third ray is the orange ray (right boundary of shaded sector). Next, the left boundary of the shaded sector: the ray at 85° + shaded angle. The 40° angle is between the left boundary ray and OA (180°). So left boundary ray is 180° - 40° = 140°. Therefore shaded sector is from 85° to 140°, which is 55°.

Check: sum of upper half: 20+30+35+55+40 = 180. Good.

Therefore shaded angle = 55°. Probability = 55/360 = 11/72.

Simplify: 55/360 = 11/72.

Thus answer: \boxed{11/72}.
content:
Looking at the upper half of the disk (from B to A, totaling 180°), the angles from OB are: 20°, 30°, 35°, then the shaded sector, then 40° up to OA.

Shaded angle = 180° − (20° + 30° + 35° + 40°) = 180° − 125° = 55°.

Probability = shaded sector area / total disk area = 55° / 360° = 11/72.

\boxed{11/72}
